svg.text: What uses memory during a search
Example numbers, except where stated. One square = 1 MB of the 256 MB Java heap.
• The tokenizer dictionary (loaded at the first search)
Native memory · not counted in the 256 MB
• The text model (a file mapped into memory)
On disk, not in memory: the photos, and library.json (≈ 22–28 MB).
Today: a search on a full heap

g.text: 1. An analysis starts. It reads the whole library file at
+ Appears: the text of the file, all at once (40 cells)
2. The analysis turns this text into a tree of objects and
keeps it for its whole run: 60 more cells.
− Disappears: nothing: the text is still there
3. While the analysis runs, you open the Search screen:
the library is decoded again, 150 cells. 250 of 256 used.
+ Appears: the library records, for the search (150 cells)
− Disappears: nothing: the analysis still holds its text and tree
4. You type 'gaufres'. The dictionary tries to load: 70
+ Appears: the dictionary (70 cells, 64 of them refused, in red)
− Disappears: everything ChatLab had in memory
1. The file is read in pieces: one piece of 2 cells at a
+ Appears: one piece of the file (2 cells)
2. The 768 numbers of each photo go into one block: 9
− Disappears: nothing: the piece is still there
3. Dates and paths are kept in a light form: 10 cells
4. The piece is freed. The library now takes 19 cells.
− Disappears: the piece of the file
5. You type 'gaufres'. The compact dictionary: 25 cells
6. Ranking keeps only the 10 best photos: 5 cells.
7. Results are shown. 49 of 256 cells used: there is room

svg.text: text of the file (read at once)
refused: does not fit in the 256 cells
